sanjay: Quick smoke — running apples-to-apples synthetic vs replay on gcp-a100 (driver 510) and gcp-a100 (driver 525). Kernel selector picks fast_attn_v2 on 525 but falls back to baseline kernels on 510. Seeing steady 12-18% p50 latency delta and KV cache miss spikes during longer chats. Anyone else hit this?
maria: Which image + CUDA combo? could be a kernel build flag difference or libc mismatch.
sanjay: Using images: `redwood/inference:v2026-03-01-cuda11.7` on 510 and `redwood/inference:v2026-03-09-cuda12.1` on 525. We tried forcing the same image on both but driver mismatch prevented fast_attn load on 510.
aj: Are you running the replay harness with the same trace? synthetic traffic can hide KV cache churn.
sanjay: Yep same trace (prod-chat-replay-2026-02-20). Replay config attached inline:```bash --replay --trace prod-chat-replay-20260220.json --kv-mode=shared --batching=continuous --max-seqlen=2048 ```
dana: Can you paste the kernel selector logs? I want to see why fast_attn_v2 is rejected on 510. Often it's a check for `cupti` or a compute capability mismatch.
sanjay: snippet from runtime logs:```kernel_selector: candidate fast_attn_v2 -> rejected (cuBlasLt missing) candidate fast_attn_v1 -> accepted selected kernel: fast_attn_v1```
maria: cuBlasLt missing usually indicates CUDA runtime mismatch at container/driver boundary. On 510 we installed cuda11.7 libs in container but host driver lacks required symbols introduced in 525. That explains fallback.
aj: That fallback explains latency but shouldn't explain KV cache miss spikes. Are there prefetch threads starving under continuous batching? Check `kv_fetch_ms` distribution in profiler.
sanjay: profiler excerpt shows tail during replay: `kv_fetch_ms: p50=0.9ms p95=4.8ms p99=12.2ms` on 525 vs `p50=1.1ms p95=9.6ms p99=28.0ms` on 510.
dana: Larger tail on 510 could be GC pauses or different NUMA binding. Are containers pinned to GPUs with `--cpuset-cpus`? Also kernel flags? we recently toggled `sched_wakeup_granularity` in the image for a test.
maria: We should run the same container image + runtime flags, and if driver blocks fast kernels, explicitly record that as a config delta. For apples-to-apples we need: image tag, host driver, kernel flags, cpuset, and CUDA visible devices.
sanjay: Agreed. Proposed checklist for next run: 1) Same image on both hosts 2) Record `nvidia-smi -q` and `uname -a` 3) Force kernel flag set file `/proc/sys/kernel/sched_wakeup_granularity_ms` 4) Run both synthetic and replay traces 5) Capture `kernel_selector.log`, `perf` lightweight counters, and profiler flamegraphs. Anyone want to take ownership?
aj: I can run 510 hosts with forced cuda libs shim to emulate 525 symbols and run the harness. Will log kernel_selector + KV metrics.
dana: I'll audit image build: check compile flags used for fast_attn (AVX/arch flags) and the container glibc. Also validate our entrypoint doesn't override `CPUS_ALLOWED`.
maria: I'll extend the replay harness to add a deterministic ramp-up and annotate events where model fallback occurs — makes correlation easier.
perf-bot: smoke-run-1978888888: finished 6 runs each (synthetic,replay) on drivers {510,525}. Summary: 525 median token-latency 13% lower; KV cache tail p99 reduced 55% on 525. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/smoke/1978888888/*.tgz
sanjay: Thanks all — next steps: aj -> run emulated symbol shim on 510 and post logs, dana -> image compile flags audit, maria -> harness annotation. We'll re-run by EOD UTC and sync results here. :thumbsup:
